lines:
Fixed in cdd24ba, together with task 144's implementation. The recorded diagnosis was wrong and the real cause is different, so both are recorded here.

THE RECORDED HYPOTHESIS IS DISPROVEN. FrozenModelGateway owns its providers in a Vec (crates/aworkit-capability-host/src/model.rs) and the fixture builds one per test; there is no process-wide binding registry, and `ephemeral_semantic_event_committer()` returns a fresh Arc per call, so the fixtures do not share an event store either. Adding distinct binding ids would have changed nothing.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS. Instrumented the failing tests with entry/exit probes. In a failing run `manage_model_context` left the request untouched (the hash at entry equalled the hash at both exits), while the test's `before` hash - taken before the call - differed. The difference is created by the pre-loop preparation: `restore_context` / `state_context` / `workspace_context`. A wider probe showed exactly what was gained: a fourth context message, `record.workspace-instructions.94c15ec4...`, 479 chars, "\\n<system-reminder>\\nTrusted Aworkit host clock for the latest user turn..." - the trusted host-clock reminder, injected per user turn. So the request legitimately changes during preparation, and a whole-request hash is simply not a valid change detector. That is also why it was intermittent and load-dependent: under parallel load the clock injection lands on the other side of the test's snapshot boundary. Single-threaded runs never failed; the module in parallel failed in roughly one run in five and always in the two tests that returned ProviderError::RequestTimedOut (their fixtures ran longest before the second preparation).

THE FIX. The contract is now asserted through the committed evidence, with a shared helper `assert_no_reduction(f, changed, context)`: a failed or cancelled compaction must not mark the selection changed and must commit no `context.compacted` event. Applied to `failed_cancelled_and_nonshrinking_summaries_leave_the_selection_unchanged`, `an_exhausted_summary_recovery_warns_once_and_keeps_the_selection` and `cancellation_wins_over_summary_recovery`, replacing `assert_eq!(c::hash(&request), before)` and `assert_eq!(request, before)`. The provider-call-count and warning assertions are unchanged. No binding ids were touched, because they were never the problem.

VERIFICATION. Ten consecutive parallel runs of the previously flaky filter (`-- recovery --test-threads=8`): all green, where the same command failed in roughly one run in five before. Eleven clean full-suite runs at 488 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

PRODUCTION NOTE, deliberately not changed here: the host-clock reminder being injected during preparation is by design (one reminder per user turn), so nothing in the runtime is wrong; what was wrong was a test asserting a whole-request identity across a boundary that is documented to add per-turn context. If the clock's injection point itself ever needs to be deterministic for another reason, that belongs to the workspace-instructions element, not here.

ALSO RECORDED: a rare *hang* of the whole suite (once in twelve full-suite runs, all 24 threads blocked on futexes for 15 minutes with no compaction test in flight) is a separate observation with its own task.

Observed once while finishing task 143 (number 142), unrelated to the policy change and not reproduced since.

With the whole desktop lib suite in parallel (484 tests), runtime::tool_loop::workspace_instructions::tests::compaction_integration::an_exhausted_summary_recovery_warns_once_and_keeps_the_selection failed at its first assertion, assert!(prepared.provider_error.is_some()), while its gateway unconditionally returns ProviderError::RequestTimedOut. It passes when run alone and passed on every full-suite rerun afterwards, including three consecutive runs of the whole compaction_integration module.

Suspected cause: every test in desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/compaction/integration_tests.rs builds its gateway with the same binding id "model.compaction-test" and version hash "v1" (see fn gateway in that file). If FrozenModelGateway installs into a process-wide registry keyed by binding id, a parallel sibling test registering the same id can serve the request instead, so a compaction that should have failed succeeds and provider_error stays None. A second candidate is the shared ToolRecordStore/committer path in Fixture, but each fixture uses its own tempfile directory.

Work: give each test a distinct binding id (or version hash) so a registry collision cannot occur, or make registration assert on duplicate ids so the collision is loud, then run the whole lib suite repeatedly to show the flake is gone. Acceptance: 10 consecutive full-suite runs, no failure in that test; a duplicate binding id is an error rather than a silent override.

data.title: Compaction tests flake under parallelism: every fixture registers the same gateway binding id
